key_insight: An adaptive confidence-gated decoder can combine a fast neural network with selective MWPM refinement to improve rotated-surface-code decoding accuracy while keeping latency low.
engineering_relevance: This design is relevant for real-time quantum error correction because it targets the key hardware bottleneck: high-throughput, low-latency decoding on commodity compute resources.
method: Fast-path decoding with a lightweight feed-forward neural network.
Low-confidence syndrome predictions are escalated to MWPM refinement.
Benchmarking across rotated surface codes with distances d=3,5,7,9,11 under circuit-level depolarising noise.
evidence_signal: At a 0.95 confidence threshold, only 3.3%–6.2% of syndromes were sent to refinement, improving logical accuracy from 99.21% to 99.81% with bounded extra decoding cost.
watch_item: Results are validated on simulated Stim benchmarks, so hardware integration, timing jitter, and end-to-end system overhead may change the observed latency gains.
paper_title: Latency-Constrained Hardware-Aware Quantum Error Correction Co-Design with Adaptive Confidence-Gated Neural Decoding for the Rotated Surface Code
